reviews.text: 画风很棒，但是游戏设置有些不合理 1.敌人进攻节奏很快，高费卡很难发挥效果 2.全程靠那几张强力单卡，拿到就过关，拿不到就危险了 3.不能使用鼠标操作，很麻烦 我服了，更新完出bug了，升级以后退出游戏，再进去又会回到升级之前，就像没升级一样。 跟新以后问题还是没有解决，退出以后升级就没了，又回到之前的状态。 bug修复了，但是怪物还是太离谱，难度0的情况下，100血的士兵被瞬杀，对面boss直接平推。
难度曲线做得一坨，前中后费用都一样，纯靠超模怪，翻译稀烂，成就没有翻译还是韩文，还不如demo的时候好玩，打最后橡树的时候纯拖时间，近战被boss一下秒，纯靠远程给boss刮痧

内容很少，很快就打完了2个角色的首通，当然这是小问题，游戏的难度曲线和玩家成长做的非常离谱。 初始卡组弱到爆炸，出门的远程松鼠才多少射程没点数吗，就这还没有近战aoe远的射程也配叫远程兵？数量完全堆不起来。近战兵更是抽象中的抽象，就那一丢丢血条花2费出他都是我没脑子。 当然我也没考虑过用初始卡组打穿游戏，玩家怎么变强呢？我们想想其他卡牌游戏是怎么做的，是用能力牌强化自己，或者组建牌组转来转去。 这游戏里几乎完全没有能力牌，给兵种的buff在士兵死后就消失，导致玩小兵想要压制boss就只能堆小兵数量，然后被boss一发aoe带走。 至于转来转去，我承认是这个游戏里最好赢的了，不管是转游鼠还是转墓碑都很好赢。为什么？他们有“打出此牌后下一次数值＋1”这个高贵的词条！简单刷一会就能压制boss。 同理，刷很多凤凰（死后3秒在基地复活，遗物10%多复活1只）以及特定遗物（带星号的动物死后减1费）特别好赢，就因为他们有局内成长，现在基本只能靠这个赢。 你要低人一等也可以玩小猪（每次死亡永久加3血），比上面的墨迹很多但是终究是能玩的。 为什么就这些赢点？这类游戏的正常玩法不该是爆兵压制对面吗？对不起，boss的各种远程近战aoe分分钟清掉你累死累活堆出来的小兵数量，然后对面堆人海玩家没有aoe去处理，当然就会直接去世。 最后吐槽一下，玩家本体屁用没有，换王冠堆射程花里胡哨一点卵用没有，玩家在战场上的影响约等于0。能抓的法术牌更是幽默至极，我花那么多费用给士兵加buff，士兵被打死就等于0，然后2个职业加起来凑不出一张解场牌，唯一aoe还是初始职业的初始卡，还tm只打2。 希望后续更新能处理这些问题吧，感觉当务之急是给玩家侧添加aoe清兵技能，以及永续生效的局内成长能力，没有这些的话这游戏已经到头了，后续出新角色新关卡怎么都逃不开这类套路

I really liked the game. Beat it in a day. It's like Battle Cats except it has a much deeper strategy, more creative creatures, and no micro transaction. I probably played it for 7 1/2 hours. It says ten, but I went out to dinner with my family and left it on pause. I see that some people seem to dislike the game. I can't see their reasons as I don't speak the same language as all of the negative reviews. Anyway, it was fun. I hope they have some better luck. Correction: I made an incorrect statement regarding the lack of mouse/keyboard controls. It looks like they have regular keyboard/mouse controls.

目前玩了五小时，刚开始难度0反而是最难的，一是不熟悉游戏，二是一些强力卡不熟悉或者没解锁，当打通一两次游戏，其他更高难度反而次次能通，初始卡组过于废物，基本没有培养的必要，也没必要太在意精简卡组，高费的卡也不一定强，带个初始卡组也能通关高难度，这游戏是可以sl的，多去拿遗物，尤其是有几个成长型的卡牌，还有一个复制狗，看着属性不强，但是承伤和伤害次次最高，最后一两波来个复制，强度拉满， 说下优点：demo的时候就被吸引了，一是画风可爱，二是操行难度低，但是也考验卡组构建以及打牌的思路，这游戏居然也是能完成无限的（技能卡后出兵加一费，出兵后出技能卡加一费，拿低费卡组无限刷），三是缝合怪，有多种机制加强卡牌，带帽子升级卡强化怪物遗物，可能才双角色通过难度五六，每场还是挺新奇的。 缺点是：一初始卡组太弱，近战远程都是低血低攻，屯不起来，不熟悉游戏被怪清场后反推，堵在家里出不去，二是单一，卡牌单一，怪物单一，目前最后一关都是树，卡组容易挑着熟悉的那一两个卡牌，等到打通最高难度，估计不会再玩了。三是英雄没太大特色，甚至没什么用，第一个是给加加移速，不能打不能抗，第二好一点，有很多咒术可以配合。 个人还是觉得值得一玩的，也玩了很多肉鸽卡牌，希望制作组多出一点特色怪，不要只有数值
不推荐，整体而言太过于吃随机性了下一把和上一局比都没有形成“我这个角色更强了”的感觉，升级给与的提升更是微乎其微，仅仅只是解锁了部分卡牌（或许这些卡牌很强，但是它们不一定能到我的手上啊），难度提升太快，基本上和试玩版区别不大。
15个小时不到打完难度10了，基本都是靠反伤和堆血量打赢的，最奇葩的是，远程堆攻击压根就没用，BOSS一发AOE就死了，要堆血量，靠数量磨过去。高费卡相当鸡肋，狐狸是必拿卡，复制或怎么样都要搞到3-4只，前期早上找准主养的角色（小猪，刺猬、游豚都可以）看到合适的帽子、护符再给BUFF。奶妈完全是陷阱，看到就跳过，自从看到一直给几乎满血的浣熊一直奶，就觉得这玩意就是个废物

底子很好，但目前数值和流派数量都不太行。不同build的成型难度和强度不成正比，比如猴子套路无敌强，需要的组件也很容易找到，一个好帽子和一个强化就能转起来，甚至还非常适应各种魔法和护符，有没有猴子专属护符都无所谓。而其他的套路需要很多互相配合的卡，随从帽子法术护符都要能互相配合否则夜晚都过不去。 ----------------诅咒10通关更新----------- 一旦选定流派，无用强化太多，关卡中一大半的奖励都需要放弃，希望制作组可以找到更合理利用资源的办法。 某一级诅咒开始，旅鼠这些1攻击友军在白天关卡不拿舍不得，拿了=0攻击力，高级诅咒的boss数值又高，少一个友军打击太大。除了加护甲咱还可以多想想别的加难度的方式，不要一杆子把低攻随从打死。比如环境、卡位限制，开点脑洞，多点可以通过操作来应对的难度内容，像“每召2个随从，下1个被削弱”。别搞这么无聊

一开始就被游戏可爱的画风吸引了，感觉蠢萌蠢萌的，游戏流程不算长，玩了十多个小时就全成就了，游戏的质量很不错，小品级别的游戏内容很丰富，肉鸽的玩法也让游戏有重复游玩的乐趣，不过还是有几个建议，希望制作组可以采纳。首先是游戏的主角几乎没有成长，除了使用法术牌影响战局外，在游戏里没有其他可以造成实质性影响的东西，例如可以出一个角色让他在游戏内可以战斗，而随从可以反向对角色提供增益。其次就是游戏的特殊事件希望可以让玩家选择顺序，有时候很尴尬帽子事件出现在卡安事件前面，刚好刷出了好帽子但是就差几十块钱。还有就是在最终BOSS战之前可以固定安排几个花掉卡安的特殊事件，要不然决战前手上几百个卡安用不出去的情况很正常。或者可以出一个局外成长功能，一局剩下的卡安可以用于局外永久提升角色属性，或者是随从的属性。还有就是升级蘑菇塔的作用聊胜于无，其实最大作用还是可以删除一张卡牌，最后游戏的中文翻译还需要润色一下，有些翻译还是怪怪的。

比较烦的是卡组精简太难，只能永加速抽卡来缓解卡组压力，初始卡组全是垃圾，都要删。猎人不知道是不是有bug，初始帽子一换就领域变小，只有身前一厘米，都给我整笑了，近战枪手，后期怪boss怪自带减伤很难突破，而且不是每个人都有控制技能和削减伤的技能 最烦的是这个操作模式，作者也不像是没玩过卡牌游戏的啊，要不就鼠标操作，要不就单手操作，就几个键够用了呀，有时候AD能移动有时候又得上下左右才能选择卡牌，而且还不能自定义按键，作者怎么想的，没人骂你吗，是独立开发吗，开发了一年了还是就几个boss吗，哪怕全鼠标操作，我一个手抽烟吃零食也好啊

It's an OK game that gives a lot of ability to tweak your deck each play, but the meta progression is very limited. At time of writing there are only 3 characters that can go up 5 levels (each leading to 2 card unlocks). I'm giving a thumbs down because the game is short and the balance needs major adjusting. As others have stated, the difficulty ramps up on the final fight to a ridiculous degree. Over the course of the game it preps you before each fight as to what the enemies will be doing, but I never once bothered to read and figure out all the information it was unloading on me. None of that junk matters because it all simply amounts to scrub fights. Even my 10 YO can clear all that trash, usually picking the rewards based on nothing more than what provides the "cutest" animals. THEN you hit the boss battle and the mobs are stupid tanky. I did win after a few tries, so I tried another character and had what I thought was a far superior build, only taking a total of 3 damage the entire session, even healing to 100% and getting a bonus 1-time artifact going into the boss fight... yet I didn't even get 1 hit on the boss. Really?!? 95% of each play-through is a waste of time. You face off against squishy mobs, all with different mechanics that all have virtually no impact then get rewarded with several deck upgrades, artifacts and/or shop opportunities. Rinse and repeat like 8 times. Then (likely) get wiped by the final fight. Just give me my 40 minutes back and let me pick 15 cards, a dozen artifacts and have a 1000 gold shopping spree to see if I can come up with the RNG combo to get past the final HP check. My current play time is a combo of myself and my 10 YO, but I'd say after about 10 hours you'll unlock everything, see all your're going to see and have no incentive to keep playing.

OK game but frustrating. Limited progression (3 classes, 5 levels each) and the runs themselves have a LARGE spike in difficulty at the final level. It's the catapult. A catapult that will fire about once a second for 20 dmg in an area and will respawn about 5 times through the course of the fight. Most tank units will start at 60 HP with maybe a little flat dmg reduction. This means you have to 1. Find a tank that can scale to deal with it 2. Have a ridiculous amount of minion generation to pave the way with corpses or 3. Stack evasion so high that you dodge all catapult its and have a way to maintain that for 5 catapult spawns. There is also a tank unit that will spawn with double the hp and splash damage to protect said catapults. Does the game prepare you for this? Unless you already know what coming, no, not at all. You will pave through the most of it and then get a hard DPS and HP check at the end. This results in a very limited amount of cards and tactics that will be able to viably add value to the final fight. So, as of right now, I would not recommend playing this game

Game lacks intuitive controls for PC. Keyboard arrows and QWER is awkward to play with. While the first win took time, it is pretty short. By the time you find synergy between cards, it's over. I wish it were longer to fully build your cards. Card tool tips need more info or explanation on hover. There are short descriptions that cause confusion. Like, falls asleep and recovers HP when below 50%, but never tells you if they 'wake up' to continue fighting or not. They sleep to 51%? Or to 100%? Etc. Lots of cards could use fully fleshed out explanations to explain their entire process. I like that there are a lot of ways to enhance your deck, but again, it's short and doesn't feel fully reach the potential it could.

Surprisingly enjoyable. I picked Forest Heroes up randomly in a bundle and didn’t expect much, but it ended up being more fun than I thought. There are definitely things I don’t love, but overall it’s a solid, more casual take on similar deck/auto-battler hybrids. I played around 25 runs (my playtime is inaccurate because I left the game open) and completed all achievements. After that, I didn’t feel much motivation to keep going (which is fine). What I liked: The upgrade system is very satisfying, especially the unit and hat upgrades. Runs are short and snappy, which makes the game easy to pick up. What I didn’t like as much: The playable elf and crowns feel a bit underwhelming. There are many upgrade breaks between fights; I’d prefer more battles and fewer reward screens. The game is quite easy overall—probably due to the high number of upgrades and the strong draw mechanics (you can redraw every ~5 seconds and instantly draw after playing a card), which makes it simple to keep only good cards in hand. Overall, it’s a fun, lightweight game that’s worth trying if you want something casual—but don’t expect long-term depth. Edit: After reading other reviews, I want to add that yes, the control scheme is really weird. Not having a mouse + WASD option is honestly puzzling. I’m confused about people saying the game gets hard near the end though. The only explanation I can think of is that players let their deck get too big. That doesn’t scale well—keep your deck small, skip rewards and remove bad cards. I always found the first 3 fights to be the "hardest" or rather annyoing since the starting deck is pretty rough, but once you pick up even ~2 good cards, the rest becomes easy because you can recycle them fast or buff them with spells.

Scaling builds win. Other builds are pointless. There is very little incentive to taking cards other than the few that scale hard. Once you get one of these cards, the run is an inevitable win, so you're just going through the motions for the rest of it. This heavily limits card usability and leads to a fairly flat experience; most scalers focus on repeatedly playing them, so it's not worth filling your deck with junk. ~90% of cards aren't worth taking. I can only imagine the dev laughed when they put in the little winmore/losemore thing in front of the base (which gives you a relic in exchange for getting obliterated if your deck isn't already a guaranteed win).

I think the point that its pretty easy to break this game is pretty valid. The best builds typically either center around being able to spam allies through cost reduction effects, or builds that buff your allies significantly, etc. but I don't think that's necessarily bad. It's similar to Battle Cats in a way, where you generate resources to spend on cards to defend your tower, and your units move. You also have your own unit that can move and perform actions through cards that can heal. attack, or buff your minions. There are 3 different classes you can unlock each with a bit more specialization and unique abilities compared to the others, with the first class being an all rounder with character spells that typically buff your allies, deal damage and knockback, or multiply them. The necromancer class is unique in that she produces graves when allies die, and with spells, and these graves can be used to pay off cards or produce allies on the spot rather than wait for them to spawn from your tower. Her spells can also cost her own health to buff allies as well. This class plays better into cards that scale off ally deaths, since the grave minions are quite disposable. The last class is a hunter class that can actually do consistent damage with bullets, or buff allies using a "bird" flying mode. Ultimately its just better to spam evade buffs with this class haha, but going for a gun-centric build can be ridiculously funny as well. You can kinda see which animals best fit certain classes, but truthfully any animal that can scale permanently, gain attack speed, range, or be spammed will likely win you the game. In difficulty modifier modes, some paths will even have more resources to upgrade your deck to compensate you for harder difficulty, but that makes it also easier to tune into a broken animal build. Despite all these "flaws" I still think that for $10 you can get some decent fun out of this game. I occasionally jump back in, discover a fairly unique build, and the game is forgiving enough to make it work. You will find yourself typically choosing similar artifacts per run especially early because so much is locked behind progression, which makes the early game feel samey. If the game goes on sale, and you like Battle Cats and making busted builds, I recommend it, its kinda more a cozy game to me. If you are ok with this not being an absolutely hard-core difficulty experience, I'd say try the demo and see if you enjoy the gameplay loop.

Play Time: 27.8hrs Achievements: 22 out of 23 achievements (250 Mana left.. lets see how long it takes me to get this) Date of original review: July 3rd 2026 Rating: 7 1/3 Forest Heroes: is a “tug of war” game where it's about using your character, animal friends, and spells to beat the evil plants. Nothing more ironic then beating a massive tree with a ton of Acorns. The game comes with 56 allies, 237 Artifacts (aka passives that impact your run), 53 Hats to equipment onto your allies, 17 crowns your character can wear. And of course you have skill cards you can obtain and use. They are unique to your character. You'll come across 15 different difficulties, all of which offer a new challenge for you. In your travel of tug of war you'll encounter the plant baddies whom are semi unique and have different abilities that will impact how you summon or create your allies. On your journey you'll chose either the left side for events or the right side for events. This tiny but very impact decision making can make a difference in every run. P.S. This is very much so a keyboard game. QWER, and arrows. Characters you can play: 3 unique characters that have their own unique play style. These characters will synchronize with animals and builds in different ways based on their skill cards and passives. Each character also has an Allie that works best with them, and are almost useless if you encounter them with another character. Artifacts: 237 Artifacts makes a huge world of difference, and sometimes they just synchronize with eachother and your allies. Artifacts make up a lot of how your build is going to work. The best way to explain them is are they balanced NO, but do they all for the most part make a difference YES. And instead of them having a negative effect on you, you may just have an artifact or two that don't really help your team. Enemies: You'll fight many unique enemies some of which can almost counter your builds. You won't run into them all the time, and some of the bosses you can beat them in different ways than you think. This I found out around difficulty 6, I just so happened to run into a few strategies with a character to beat a boss differently than the previous difficulties. Difficulties: Like most rogue like there is a learning curve to this game, it isn't steep but you will have to commit some time to it. There are over 15 difficulties they each will bring a unique challenge to every fight. And they are minor, in fact I like this method of challenge as compared to “all items or artifacts also have a negative impact”. To go up in difficulty you have to beat the previous difficulty with the same character. Meaning to reach difficulty 15 on all 3 characters you'll have to start from 1 work your way up to 15 on every character. Skills/Abilities: Each character has unique skills and abilities. This is probably why each difficulty level is tied to just the character you beat it on. One you may find play styles you may like with other characters, and two you have to learn builds that will work with them. Honestly I found MANY builds that worked even in the highest difficulties. Random Events & Music: The event decision making was fun, and I never felt like I had a bad option, everything was situational and the as a player I would just have to use my best guess as to what would be the best option for what I'm going for. I liked the variety, granted some events I rarely saw. Music, I can't really say it's ok, it's not amazing. Allies: I love the variety absolutely amazing. And hey this isn't no MOBA or whatever. Balance isn't always going to be perfect and with this game that's absolutely fine. You can synchronize builds that you wouldn't even think of with some allies. For example I think I was on Difficulty 13 and my primary source of damage was the Starting Sling Shot Allie. Yes the first ranged allies you start with, they were my primary source of damage. Same with the starting Raccoons, I've made builds around them. You just have to find what works, and the artifacts will help.
